title: keybindingspage
summary: MSUI's preserved standalone 1.12-style Key Bindings shell is entirely seated by KeyBindingsUiLaw and hosts current Benilla's collapsed-by-default category behavior plus live category/command search. The visible registry now follows Benilla's Movement, Chat, Action Bar, Targeting, Interface, Miscellaneous, Camera and unified MultiActionBar header order; Sheath and Toggle UI sit under their reference categories instead of the previous Interface catch-all. The window minimum, search text inset, row progression and row hit size join the existing frame, art, keys, scrollbar, feedback, checkbox and footer geometry in the law; title/column/category/command/key-capsule text now uses the authored GameFont objects, and the renderer contains no locally authored Vector2 geometry. It captures, displays, persists and dispatches canonical ALT/CTRL/SHIFT keyboard, BUTTON3/4/5 and MOUSEWHEELUP/DOWN chords, ignores modifier-only and Super captures, and steals exact chords with the reference red fully-unbound warning or success feedback. Mouse buttons use the same held edge latch as keys; wheel chords are one-frame pulses, and UI mouse ownership blocks gameplay dispatch while the armed page still captures them. Character Specific Key Bindings creates an isolated GUID-keyed set immediately; destructive uncheck springs back and routes the exact confirmation through the shared popup slots before loading the account set and deleting the character set. CharacterBindingsUiLaw owns that dynamic popup's complete size, text-line and button geometry, leaving its ImGui host with no local Vector2 seats. Focused and full clinical checks pass; live visual/input verification remains.

openItems.text: No modifier-chord capture: FirstBindableKeyDown binds bare keys only - ALT-/CTRL-/SHIFT-key combinations cannot be bound
openItems.resolution: 2026-08-22: Capture ignores standalone modifiers, samples held ALT/CTRL/SHIFT with the first non-modifier base key, rejects Super, displays canonical prefix order, and writes BindingChord values into the selected primary/secondary slot. Focused clinical checks pass.

openItems.text: No mouse button (3/4/5) or mouse-wheel binding capture
openItems.resolution: 2026-08-22: BindingChord now represents current Benilla's BUTTON3/4/5 and MOUSEWHEELUP/DOWN tokens with the same ALT/CTRL/SHIFT prefix order, persistence codec, friendly display, fallback and conflict-steal semantics as keyboard chords. ClientWindow exposes the three bindable mouse buttons plus a world-owned wheel delta. The binding runtime edge-latches held mouse buttons, pulses wheel commands for one update, and suppresses pointer dispatch while ImGui owns the mouse; the armed page captures the same inputs and does not scroll its list when the wheel is being bound. Focused chord and full interface clinical checks pass.

openItems.text: Character Specific Key Bindings checkbox is cosmetic: _characterSpecificBindings is never read by SaveBindings/LoadBindings - no per-character binding set exists
openItems.resolution: 2026-08-22: The active set is selected from account keybindings.json or a stable LocalPlayerGuid-keyed character file. Checking immediately persists a copy as the character set. Unchecking springs back, plays the reference checkbox sound and opens the exact shared StaticPopup; acceptance loads the account set before deleting the character file and re-saving the unchanged account set. Focused clinical checks pass.

openItems.text: Stealing a key silently unbinds its previous owner with no KEY_UNBOUND_ERROR-style red warning naming the victim
openItems.resolution: 2026-08-22: Exact-chord steals identify previous owners before removal. If the victim loses its final key the page displays the victim's binding label in a four-second red 'Function is Now Unbound!' warning; otherwise it displays the reference success feedback.

openItems.text: Focused chord capture, display, conflict, rule-owned shell geometry, exact category order/grouping and category/search source fences pass. Needs owner-run live capture of single and multi-modifier keyboard/BUTTON3/4/5/wheel chords, modifier-only/Super refusal, held-button and wheel-pulse action dispatch, UI mouse-ownership blocking, collapsed-category toggles, search filtering/scroll clamping, unified MultiActionBar expansion, dual-slot steals, visible red victim naming, Cancel rollback and Okay persistence.

Focused persistence-order, GUID filename, checkbox spring-back, source-exact text and shared StaticPopup geometry/lifecycle checks pass. Needs owner-run live acceptance for create/edit/reload, Cancel behavior, confirmed account restoration, character-file deletion, dead-state refusal and two-slot modal seating.
Category headers are plain labels - no collapse/expand sections and no binding search
openItems.resolution: 2026-08-22: KeyBindingsUiLaw owns the preserved 640x512 shell, search, 535x390 list viewport, 23px rows, key capsules, scrollbar, checkbox, feedback and footer seats. Categories initialize collapsed, use the stock 16px QuestLog plus/minus dress, expand on header click, and contribute children only while open. The law-seated search matches category or command labels case-insensitively, forces matching groups open, resets/clamps scrolling, and yields back to the remembered collapsed tree when cleared. Focused and full interface clinical checks pass.

openItems.text: The preserved standalone Key Bindings shell still drew its title, column labels, category headers and command rows through raw ImGui font sizes, while its key capsules inherited the generic 12px panel-button fonts instead of the current page's GameFontHighlightSmall/GameFontDisableSmall face.
openItems.resolution: KeyBindingsUiLaw owns each font identity and the current header icon/text insets. GameLoop.Keybindings uses GameText throughout, and the shared panel-button host accepts an optional law-selected font family without altering default callers. Focused BindingChord and full desktop clinical suites pass; the intentionally preserved standalone shell and all binding behavior remain unchanged.
